item.title: Variety Days for Technical Proficiency, “In-between” Strength, and Resilience | StrongFirst
item.description: I usually strength train three times a week—a minimalistic program of two to three kettlebell, barbell, or dumbbell “big lifts,” with medium/heavy weights. I follow the same program with the same lifts for a couple of months, sometimes a couple of years, meet the goal, and then switch to something else.

item.title: The Royal Road to Strength, Part 1: Kettlebell Lifter’s Travel Roadblocks | StrongFirst
item.description: At the turn of the 21st century, Dr. Randall Strossen, American strength and physical culture advocate and publisher, observed that “it is easier to find honest arm measurements than a kettlebell.”

item.title: The Royal Road to Strength, Part 2: Exploring the Lost Art of Dumbbell Lifting | StrongFirst
item.description: Years ago, I acquired a full set of dumbbells and asked one of my good friends, a former bodybuilding champion, to show me how to use them properly. We did the usual drills you see in commercial gyms: seated presses, lateral raises, flyes, triceps extensions, and of course… curls. You’ve done the same. Admit it.

item.title: The Royal Road to Strength, Part 3: Enter the Dumbbell! | StrongFirst
item.description: Around 1909, Alan Calvert’s Milo Barbell Company rolled out a universal weapon against weakness—the large-size Milo Triplex Combination Bell. One system, many options: barbell, dumbbell, and a pair of kettlebells from the same kit.

item.title: Abs, Strong First | StrongFirst
item.description: You tried high reps. You went for the “burn.” It did not work. Why do you insist on doing the same thing and expect a different outcome?

item.title: Strong by Choice: From Self-Doubt to Sinister | StrongFirst
item.description: I entered adulthood convinced I wasn’t good at sports—and never would be. I didn’t grow up with any inspiring role models, and my experience with physical education at school didn’t exactly spark a love for movement. Physical activity simply wasn’t part of my world.

item.title: My First Campaign as a StrongFirst Team Leader | StrongFirst
item.description: This reflection captures the lessons, challenges, and victories I’ve experienced during my first term as a StrongFirst Certified Team Leader. I share them in the service of the teachers and students who are carrying our school forward.

item.title: All Roads Lead to the Kettlebell Snatch Test | StrongFirst
item.description: The proverb, “All roads lead to Rome,” is recognized worldwide, appearing in countless languages and cultures. No matter how it is spoken, the meaning remains the same: there are many paths that can all lead to the same destination. The phrase has survived through centuries because it captures a universal truth: people may take different approaches, yet they often work toward a common outcome.

item.title: Conquering the Beast | StrongFirst
item.description: ...the Beast was tamed. It was a culmination of seven years of perseverance, failures, adaptations, and triumphs.

item.title: Rebuilding to a Chin-up with “The Beast” | StrongFirst
item.description: Injuries stink. Nobody likes them. Yet they are an inevitable part of life. Regardless of whether someone is mostly sedentary or highly active, injuries are bound to happen at some point. For people who are active, the biggest frustration is often not the injury itself, but the inability to do their chosen activity (or activities) at the level they would like to do them.
